sketch: Materially different from RUS with one ancilla: use ancilla-free exact synthesis over Z[1/sqrt2, i]. Steps: (1) Given target Rz(theta) or a single-qubit U (via ZYZ Euler angles into three z-rotations conjugated by H/S), fix precision eps. (2) For each z-rotation, randomly sample a candidate integer pair (u,t) in Z[omega] with |u - e^{-i theta/2}| < eps/2 inside the small eps-disc region, and require the norm equation |u|^2+|t|^2=2^k to be solvable, i.e. 2^k - |u|^2 = |t|^2 must be a norm from Z[omega], tested by probabilistic factoring (Miller-Rabin primality test plus randomized solution of x^2+y^2=p over primes). This runs in expected polynomial classical time in log(1/eps) because primes have constant density 1/log. (3) Build the unitary matrix [[u,-t*],[t,u*]]/sqrt2^k exactly. (4) Apply Kliuchnikov-Maslov-Mosca exact synthesis to decompose it into a Clifford+T word of T-count about 3 log2(1/eps) + O(log log(1/eps)) (here 3 log2(1/eps) is the abstract's ancilla-free reference bound). (5) The circuit is a measurement-free, bound unitary in standard gates h, s, t, tdg, x and similar, and its distance to the target is at most eps by construction. The claim of polynomial classical runtime is addressed, but the circuit does not itself reach the 2.5x lower expected T-count of the RUS approach. This is a baseline-style comparator that achieves the polynomial-time synthesis part of the claim, not the T-count reduction. Output decoding: act on a single data qubit, compare the simulated unitary to the target up to global phase using operator-norm or diamond-norm distance.
